payload.author: recovery-worker
evidence: Decoded image tables: trans index bytes at 0x0062AF08 / handlers at 0x0062AEF0 and opaque index at 0x0062AF30 / handlers at 0x0062AF18 map cases 4, 0xb, 0xc, 0x12 to 0x0062AEA1 (fseek chunk->size_-6 then the shared delta-correction tail), same target as the out-of-range ja; real handlers are 7, 0xd, 0xf, 0x10.
Compiled /O2 switch bounds from deck-chunk baseline: add eax,-7; cmp eax,9 (span [7,0x10]) with fall-through labels 4/0xb/0xc/0x12 dropped; candidate size 608 vs original 541.

deck-chunk2 measurement: case-4-fseek (explicit fseek per label plus default) compiled 656 under both flag sets (+48 = two extra un-merged fseek bodies), fused-end (size + ftell - 6) is a size plateau (608/624 unchanged, robust a-6 CSE reassoc), rect-locals ties baseline; all lost_passing_measurements empty.
payload.hypothesis: The original decode_chunk spelled the FLI subchunk skip labels (4, 0xb, 0xc, 0x12) as explicit case entries in both switches, not fall-throughs to default: the image's jump tables are dense over [4,0x12] with those four cases routed to the same fseek(size-6) handler as out-of-range, while VC6 fed a fall-through spelling folds them away (table span [7,0x10], compiled 608/624 vs image 541). Duplicating the fseek body per label keeps a wide table but emits un-merged call sites (+48 bytes, 656), proving VC6 does not tail-merge; no idiomatic spelling among those measured reproduces the image's wide table plus single shared body.
